title: Solubility changes without changing Ksp
promptMarkdown: A hypothetical salt MA(s) dissociates as M⁺+A⁻ with dimensionless Ksp=1.00×10⁻⁸. HA has Ka=1.00×10⁻⁵. An external buffer maintains pH3.00; assume ideal dilute activities, c°=1M, no other complexes and excess solid. (a) Combine dissolution and protonation reactions to find K for MA+H⁺⇌M⁺+HA. (b) Derive the fraction α of dissolved A present as A⁻ and calculate total solubility s, [A⁻] and [HA]. (c) Compare with the formal α=1 limit. (d) Identify what must change in the calculation for a finite-capacity or absent buffer.
hintLadder: Add dissolution to reverse acid dissociation.
Use total dissolved A=s and Aminus/HA=Ka/h.
Check both mass balance and the original Ksp after solving.
